newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Clariant shares jump after trading resumes.
newsitem.headline: Clariant shares jump after trading resumes.

text.p: Shares in Swiss chemicals group Clariant AG resumed trading on the Swiss Exchange at 470 Swiss francs per share, up 11 francs or 2.3 percent, from the level the stock was trading at prior to its suspension.

Clariant's shares were suspended shortly after 1100 GMT on the company's behest following news from Frankfurt that Hoechst AG would take a sizeable minority stake in Clariant as part of a merger of the two companies' speciality chemicals businesses.
Prior to its suspension, Clariant's shares were already 11 francs firmer from their Monday close of 448 francs in relative heavy trading.
After Hoechst announced the deal, a Clariant spokesman declined immediate comment.
Later, however, Clariant confirmed the deal in a statement from its Muttenz headquarters.
The merger of the two companies' speciality chemicals activities will propel Clariant, which was only spun off from Sandoz AG last year, to one of the world's leading producers.
Clariant's annual sales will almost quadruple to around eight billion Swiss francs from 2.3 billion prior to the merger.
Clariant expects the broader product range and larger regional presence to boost market opportunities and both companies expect synergy effects of several hundred million francs.
